/**
 * @generated by patterns — regenerate rather than edit.
 * @pattern context-budget
 * @options cd88a9a53f098208
 */

/**
 * Fitting a conversation into a model's context window.
 *
 * The newest turns that fit, and nothing else.
 *
 * The arithmetic is the part worth reading. A context window holds the request
 * and the reply together, so the room for the answer comes off before anything
 * is measured — a conversation weighed against the whole window fits right up
 * to the moment the model tries to answer. Two other costs are not messages and
 * are as easy to forget: the system prompt, which this port sends as a field
 * rather than a turn, and the tool schemas, which go with every request.
 *
 * Each message is its own unit here. A conversation carrying tool results needs
 * the pairing rule instead — dropping an assistant turn while keeping the
 * results that answer it produces a request every provider rejects, and this
 * file has no role to put those results in.
 *
 * Nothing here shortens a message. A truncated question is a different
 * question, so a conversation whose undroppable part is larger than the window
 * is refused rather than trimmed into one that fits.
 */

/**
 * The conversation, as the `chat-model-port` pattern's messages.
 *
 * Declared here rather than imported, so this file depends on nothing. It is
 * the same shape, which the emitted type tests state as a claim in both
 * directions: a conversation from the port can be measured, and what comes back
 * can be sent.
 *
 * There is no `system` role, because the port has none — a system prompt is a
 * field on the request. That is not a detail here: it makes the system prompt
 * the one piece of context that cannot be dropped, so it is measured as a fixed
 * cost rather than considered as a candidate.
 */

/**
 * A run of text.
 */
export interface TextPart {
  readonly type: "text";
  readonly text: string;
}

/**
 * What the caller said.
 */
export interface UserMessage {
  readonly role: "user";
  readonly content: readonly TextPart[];
}

/**
 * What the model said.
 */
export interface AssistantMessage {
  readonly role: "assistant";
  readonly content: readonly TextPart[];
}

export type Message = UserMessage | AssistantMessage;

/**
 * What has to fit, and what it has to fit into.
 *
 * Every number is in tokens, and every one of them describes the same request:
 * the window the provider allows, and the parts of that window this
 * conversation does not get to use.
 */

export interface Budget {
  /** The provider's window for this model, request and reply together. */
  readonly contextWindow: number;
  /**
   * Room to leave for the answer. Taken off the window before anything is
   * measured. Left out, a conversation is fitted against room the reply needs,
   * and the request is rejected on the way back rather than on the way out.
   */
  readonly reserveForOutput: number;
  /**
   * The system prompt, which is a field on a request rather than a message in
   * it. Measured here so a caller cannot forget it, and charged one message's
   * framing: one mainstream wire format sends it as the first message, and
   * paying for framing it does not have is the harmless direction to be wrong
   * in.
   */
  readonly system?: string;
  /**
   * What the provider adds around each message: the role, the delimiters, the
   * turn markers. A per-provider fudge factor, and small — but a conversation
   * of eighty short turns is mostly framing, so leaving it out is how a window
   * that was measured carefully still overflows.
   */
  readonly perMessageOverhead?: number;
  /**
   * How to count tokens. The provider's own tokeniser, where there is one. The
   * default is an estimate and is documented as one. Anything sized close to
   * the window wants the real thing.
   */
  readonly countTokens?: (text: string) => number;
}

/**
 * A conversation that fits, and what it cost.
 */
export interface Fitted {
  readonly kind: "fitted";
  /** The conversation to send, in order. */
  readonly messages: readonly Message[];
  /**
   * What was left out, in order. Worth logging: it is the context the model
   * will not have.
   */
  readonly dropped: readonly Message[];
  /**
   * What the request will cost: the kept messages and the system prompt.
   * `tokens + reserveForOutput` never exceeds `contextWindow`, which is the
   * invariant worth asserting in a caller's own suite.
   */
  readonly tokens: number;
}

/**
 * What cannot be dropped does not fit.
 *
 * Both numbers are in the same currency, which is the input side of the window:
 * `available` is the window less the room the reply was promised, and `needed`
 * is what the request costs with every droppable turn already gone.
 */
export interface Overflow {
  readonly kind: "overflow";
  readonly needed: number;
  readonly available: number;
}

/**
 * Either a conversation to send or the refusal to shorten a question.
 */
export type Budgeted = Fitted | Overflow;

/**
 * Fits a conversation into a budget, or says that it cannot be done.
 *
 * The newest turns that fit, and nothing else.
 *
 * Returns the `overflow` arm when what cannot be dropped does not fit. Nothing
 * is truncated to avoid that: a shortened question is a different question.
 */
export function fitToBudget(
  messages: readonly Message[],
  budget: Budget,
): Budgeted {
  const count = budget.countTokens ?? estimateTokens;
  const overhead = budget.perMessageOverhead ?? MESSAGE_OVERHEAD;

  // The reply's room comes off first. A window holds both halves of the
  // exchange, so a conversation measured against the whole of it fits until the
  // moment the model tries to answer.
  const available = budget.contextWindow - budget.reserveForOutput;

  // And these are charged before anything is chosen, because nothing below can
  // drop them: the system prompt is a field rather than a turn.
  const fixed =
    budget.system === undefined ? 0 : overhead + count(budget.system);

  // Nothing is droppable at this point, so this is the answer rather than a
  // special case of one.
  if (fixed > available) {
    return refused(fixed, available);
  }

  const units = unitsOf(messages).map((unit): Unit => ({
    messages: unit,
    tokens: unit.reduce(
      (total, message) => total + costOf(message, count, overhead),
      0,
    ),
  }));

  const chosen = select(units, available - fixed);

  if (chosen.kind === "over") {
    return refused(fixed + chosen.needed, available);
  }

  return fitted(chosen, fixed);
}

/**
 * The chosen turns, with the costs that are not turns added back in.
 */
function fitted(chosen: Chosen, fixed: number): Fitted {
  return {
    kind: "fitted",
    messages: chosen.messages,
    dropped: chosen.dropped,
    tokens: fixed + chosen.tokens,
  };
}

/**
 * Choosing which turns to send.
 */

/**
 * One message, weighed.
 */
interface Unit {
  readonly messages: readonly Message[];
  readonly tokens: number;
}

/**
 * The turns that fit, or the size of the ones that have to.
 *
 * `over` carries only what is needed, because the room it did not fit in is
 * whatever the caller passed. Discriminated by a string rather than by a
 * boolean: a boolean discriminant stops narrowing in a project with
 * `strictNullChecks` off, which is one of the strictness settings this file is
 * expected to compile under.
 */
type Chosen = {
  readonly kind: "chosen";
  readonly messages: readonly Message[];
  readonly dropped: readonly Message[];
  readonly tokens: number;
};

type Selection = Chosen | { readonly kind: "over"; readonly needed: number };

/**
 * Fills `room` with turns, newest first.
 *
 * The newest turn is pinned: it is the question, and a request without it asks
 * nothing. Everything else is offered from the newest backwards and the search
 * stops at the first turn that does not fit, rather than stepping over it to
 * reach a smaller one behind it. A conversation with a hole in it reads as
 * though those turns never happened, which is worse than one fewer turn and
 * harder to notice.
 */
function select(units: readonly Unit[], room: number): Selection {
  const newest = units.at(-1);

  if (newest === undefined) {
    return { kind: "chosen", messages: [], dropped: [], tokens: 0 };
  }

  if (newest.tokens > room) {
    return { kind: "over", needed: newest.tokens };
  }

  const keep = new Set<Unit>([newest]);
  const older = units.slice(0, -1);
  let left = room - newest.tokens;

  for (const unit of [...older].reverse()) {
    if (unit.tokens > left) break;

    keep.add(unit);
    left -= unit.tokens;
  }

  // One mainstream format requires the first message to be the user's, and a
  // window that opens part-way through an exchange reads oddly to any model.
  // The newest unit is exempt: a tool loop asking for an answer to results it
  // has just produced has nothing else to send.
  for (const unit of units) {
    if (!keep.has(unit)) continue;
    if (unit === newest || beginsWithUser(unit)) break;

    keep.delete(unit);
  }

  const kept = units.filter((unit) => keep.has(unit));

  return {
    kind: "chosen",
    messages: kept.flatMap((unit) => unit.messages),
    dropped: units
      .filter((unit) => !keep.has(unit))
      .flatMap((unit) => unit.messages),
    tokens: kept.reduce((total, unit) => total + unit.tokens, 0),
  };
}

/**
 * Whether a unit opens with the caller speaking.
 */
function beginsWithUser(unit: Unit): boolean {
  return unit.messages.at(0)?.role === "user";
}

/**
 * Groups the conversation into units that are kept or dropped whole.
 *
 * One message each, because without tool results there is nothing in a
 * conversation that has to travel with something else. The shape is kept so
 * that the pairing rule is a change to this function alone.
 */
function unitsOf(
  messages: readonly Message[],
): readonly (readonly Message[])[] {
  return messages.map((message) => [message]);
}

/**
 * What a message costs.
 */

/**
 * What one message costs: its framing, plus what its content serialises to.
 */
function costOf(
  message: Message,
  count: (text: string) => number,
  overhead: number,
): number {
  return message.content.reduce(
    (total, part) => total + count(part.text),
    overhead,
  );
}

/**
 * What the provider adds around each message, when a caller has not said.
 *
 * Small, and it is the kind of small that adds up: a conversation of eighty
 * short turns is mostly framing. The real figure is in the provider's own
 * documentation and is worth looking up.
 */
const MESSAGE_OVERHEAD = 4;

/**
 * Characters per token, for the default estimate.
 *
 * An English-prose figure. Code runs denser than prose, and a language written
 * without spaces runs much denser — CJK text is close to one token per
 * character, where this is out by a factor of four in the direction that fails.
 */
const CHARACTERS_PER_TOKEN = 4;

/**
 * Roughly how many tokens some text will cost.
 *
 * Rounded up, deliberately. An estimate that guesses low causes exactly the
 * rejection this file exists to prevent, and one that guesses high costs a turn
 * of context.
 *
 * It is an estimate, and for anything sized close to the window it is the wrong
 * tool: pass the provider's own tokeniser as `countTokens` and this is never
 * called.
 */
export function estimateTokens(text: string): number {
  return Math.ceil(text.length / CHARACTERS_PER_TOKEN);
}

/**
 * Reports a conversation whose undroppable part does not fit.
 *
 * One function, called from each place that can discover it, so that what a
 * refusal carries is decided once. Nothing here shortens anything to avoid the
 * refusal: what cannot be dropped is the system prompt and the newest turn, and
 * a shortened version of either is a different request from the one the caller
 * made.
 */
function refused(needed: number, available: number): Overflow {
  return { kind: "overflow", needed, available };
}

## context-budget-example.ts (example)

```ts
/**
 * @generated by patterns — regenerate rather than edit.
 * @pattern context-budget
 * @options cd88a9a53f098208
 */

/**
 * A support chat that has outgrown its window.
 *
 * Two calls. The first has to lose turns and shows which ones; the second is a
 * question that does not fit on its own, which is the case nothing can rescue.
 */

import { fitToBudget } from "./context-budget.js";
import type {
  AssistantMessage,
  Budget,
  Message,
  UserMessage,
} from "./context-budget.js";

/**
 * The conversation so far, and the two constructors it is written with.
 */

function said(text: string): UserMessage {
  return { role: "user", content: [{ type: "text", text }] };
}

function replied(text: string): AssistantMessage {
  return { role: "assistant", content: [{ type: "text", text }] };
}

/**
 * Six messages, oldest first.
 */
const CHAT: readonly Message[] = [
  said("hello, I am chasing an order from last week"),
  replied("happy to help. do you have the order number?"),
  said("it is A-1041, placed on the tuesday"),
  replied("that one shipped on wednesday and is due friday"),
  said("is there a tracking number for it?"),
  replied("there is: TRK-88213, on the courier's site"),
  said("and can I change the delivery address now?"),
];

/**
 * Long enough that no window in this file could hold it.
 */
const LOG = "GET /orders/A-1041 200 OK\n".repeat(40);

/**
 * The window this model has, and everything in it that the conversation does
 * not get.
 *
 * No `countTokens`, so the default estimate is used — fine for an example and
 * not for a request sized close to the edge, where the provider's own tokeniser
 * is the only honest answer.
 */
const BUDGET: Budget = {
  contextWindow: 160,
  reserveForOutput: 60,
  system: "You are a support agent. Be brief and never guess an order status.",
};

/**
 * Fitting the chat, then failing to fit a question.
 */
export function main(): void {
  const fitted = fitToBudget(CHAT, BUDGET);

  if (fitted.kind === "overflow") {
    report(
      `the chat needs ${String(fitted.needed)} tokens and has ${String(fitted.available)}`,
    );

    return;
  }

  report(
    `kept ${String(fitted.messages.length)} of ${String(CHAT.length)} messages ` +
      `for ${String(fitted.tokens)} tokens, dropping ${String(fitted.dropped.length)}`,
  );

  // The other case: a question that does not fit on its own. Nothing can be
  // dropped to make room for it, and shortening it would answer a question
  // nobody asked.
  const essay = [said(`here is the whole log: ${LOG}`)];

  const refused = fitToBudget(essay, BUDGET);

  if (refused.kind === "overflow") {
    report(
      `refused: it needs ${String(refused.needed)} tokens and has ${String(refused.available)}`,
    );
  }
}

/**
 * Where the example's output goes.
 */
function report(message: string): void {
  console.log(message);
}
```
